bull.b: Cloudflare is expanding quickly, with quarterly revenue growth of 39% and current RPO growth of 37%. This combination indicates strong customer demand and contracted revenue visibility, supporting continued scale, investment capacity, and operating leverage over the next several quarters.

Positive free cash flow alongside $5.1 billion of cash and securities gives Cloudflare meaningful financial flexibility. This liquidity can support network investment, product development, and customer growth while reducing dependence on external financing for near-term operations.

Rapid developer adoption broadens Cloudflare’s ecosystem and creates a pipeline for future paid usage across Workers and related services. Combined with enterprise expansion, this supports a land-and-expand model in which customers can add products, increase consumption, and deepen platform reliance.

bear.b: Debt has increased substantially relative to equity, leaving Cloudflare more exposed to financing costs and reducing balance-sheet flexibility. Although assets and cash generation have grown, leverage remains elevated until profitability becomes consistently positive and provides stronger support for obligations.

Cloudflare has improved materially from earlier losses but has not yet established durable GAAP profitability in the reported financial periods. Continued operating losses can constrain internally funded investment and leave earnings more sensitive to spending discipline and execution.

The decline in gross margin signals pressure on the profitability of Cloudflare’s revenue mix and delivery economics, even though the reported level remains within management’s target range. Sustained compression could limit operating leverage and reduce the benefit of strong revenue growth.
